title: Strip footing: uniform grid and one/two adaptive refinements

governing_assumptions: Unit out-of-plane thickness; half of a symmetric strip footing
GIMP with B-Bar velocity gradients and particle integration; Gaussian integration omitted by user instruction

geometry.description: Normal FootingLargeStrain plane-strain section, translated by -0.1 m: 10 by 10 soil and 1 by 2 rigid half-footing
geometry.coordinate_frame: x horizontal, y upward; symmetry at x=0; unit thickness

discretization.refinement_plan: Uniform h=0.1; L1 h=0.2/0.1; L2 h=0.4/0.2/0.1. Soil starts at four particles per initial cell direction and splits one-to-four at each refinement level. The rigid footing keeps the same 0.025 m sampling and never splits. Accumulated equivalent plastic deviatoric strain threshold 0.01 (dimensionless, native epdstrain), 100-step interval, 0.4 m buffer. The buffer applies only to material-indicator seeds; migrated split particles retain their level with 2:1 balancing without creating another buffer. Split parents are deferred at coarse/fine interfaces until every proposed child center lies in a cell at least as fine as the child; this prevents particle birth from propagating grid refinement without advection. RefineRatio=1.0 reserves all finest-grid nodes, including GIMP halos; it does not force refinement.

initial_conditions.velocity: Soil stationary; footing initially -0.02 m/s as in the original, then original 5 s ramp to -0.1 m/s

time.stability_policy: Reject a prescribed step above native CFL bound; never silently substitute a timestep

validation.observable: Maximum relative vertical contact action-reaction imbalance; comparison.json separately gates historical and adaptive force agreement
validation.evidence: Independent evaluation of saved curves and original particle/grid snapshots

invariants.basis: float64 reduction of total particle mass; splitting partitions parent mass and volume among its children

comparisons.observable: Adaptive versus uniform contact force versus measured settlement; uniform versus normal FootingLargeStrain saved results over the common settlement range
comparisons.expectation: At most 10 percent pointwise RMS, sampled peak and tail mean force errors at historical saved times (~0.25 s). Report sampled oscillation amplitudes separately for review; unfiltered peaks are diagnostic only by user request.

assumptions: 2D section of the laterally constrained 3D thin layer, with coordinates translated by -0.1 m; ghost margins removed and physical boundary locations preserved

Soil starts with four particles per coarse-cell direction; adaptive refinement splits each soil parent into four children per level. Rigid particles are not split by the native algorithm and keep identical 0.025 m sampling in all three runs.

GeoContact uses canonical cut_off=0.8, restoring the explicit reference value formerly misspelled cutoff; retain friction 0.1 and penalty [0.78,2.5]. Historical force snapshots are closer to the older unscaled normal-impulse law; compare that contact difference separately.
A single refinement threshold is used at both levels; no coarsening
Original two run phases are represented by one device callback with the same 5 second ramp and held terminal velocity
Historical 3D forces divided by 0.1 m thickness; compare only common settlement range

10 percent pointwise RMS, sampled peak and tail mean at historical saved times are engineering acceptance targets, not proofs of convergence; full-run volume ratios must remain in [0.5,2] and particle speeds at most 1 m/s

Refinement is driven by accumulated plastic deformation, not the earlier 500 Pa equivalent-stress trigger. The 0.01 threshold is an initial validation choice; agreement and speed must be checked against the fixed fine grid.

Use original historical saved times (~0.25 s) for force comparison, without averaging or smoothing. Report complete-cycle sampled oscillation amplitudes separately. High-frequency contact spikes are retained as diagnostics rather than pass/fail gates, as requested by the user.
